immediate_steps: Give Paracetamol 650mg immediately (adults) or 10-15mg/kg for children
Remove excess clothing — do not bundle up
Lukewarm water sponging on forehead, armpits and groin
Ensure good fluid intake — ORS, water, coconut water
Check temperature every 1 hour
do_not: Do NOT give ice cold water sponging
Do NOT give Aspirin to children under 16
Do NOT cover with heavy blankets
go_to_hospital_if: Fever above 104F (40C) not responding to medication in 1 hour
Febrile seizure (fits) occurs
Baby below 3 months has any fever
Fever with neck stiffness, rash, confusion, severe headache

immediate_steps: Give only Paracetamol for fever and pain — DO NOT give Ibuprofen or Aspirin
Ensure adequate hydration — ORS or coconut water
Monitor for warning signs closely
Get blood test: CBC with platelet count within 24-48 hours of fever onset
Rest completely
do_not: NEVER give Ibuprofen, Aspirin, or Diclofenac in dengue — increases bleeding risk severely
go_to_hospital_if: Platelet count below 100,000
Severe abdominal pain
Persistent vomiting
Bleeding from gums, nose or in urine/stool
Extreme fatigue, restlessness
Cold clammy skin

immediate_steps: Ask: Are you choking? If person cannot speak, cough or breathe — act immediately
Stand behind person, lean them forward slightly
Give 5 firm back blows between shoulder blades with heel of hand
If not cleared: stand behind, make fist above navel, grab fist with other hand, give 5 sharp upward abdominal thrusts (Heimlich manoeuvre)
Alternate 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts until object dislodged or person loses consciousness
If unconscious: call 108, start CPR
do_not: Do NOT do blind finger sweeps in mouth
Do NOT give abdominal thrusts to pregnant women or infants — use chest thrusts
go_to_hospital_if: Object was dislodged but person has difficulty breathing, swallowing or chest pain — internal injury possible

immediate_steps: Remove from heat source immediately
Cool the burn: run cool (not cold) running water over burn for 20 minutes
Remove jewellery and clothing near burn but NOT if stuck to skin
Cover loosely with clean non-fluffy cloth or cling film
Give Paracetamol or Ibuprofen for pain
do_not: Do NOT use ice, ice water, butter, toothpaste, or any home remedy on burns
Do NOT burst blisters
Do NOT remove clothing stuck to burn
go_to_hospital_if: Burns larger than palm of hand
Burns on face, hands, feet, genitals or joints
Chemical or electrical burns
Burn is deep (white/black, painless)
Child or elderly person with any significant burn

immediate_steps: Call 108 immediately — this is a medical emergency
Have person sit or lie in comfortable position — typically sitting up with knees bent
Loosen tight clothing
If conscious and not allergic: give one adult Aspirin 325mg to chew (not swallow whole) — if available
Stay with person and keep them calm
If person becomes unconscious and stops breathing: start CPR
do_not: Do NOT leave person alone
Do NOT give food or water
Do NOT let person drive themselves to hospital
go_to_hospital_if: This IS an emergency — call 108 immediately regardless
source: American Heart Association / ICMR Cardiac Emergency Guidelines

immediate_steps: If conscious: give 15-20g fast-acting sugar immediately
Options: 3-4 glucose tablets, OR half glass fruit juice, OR 3-4 teaspoons sugar in water, OR 4-5 hard candies
Recheck blood sugar after 15 minutes
If still below 70 mg/dL: repeat sugar intake
Once recovered: give a proper meal or snack
Identify why hypoglycemia occurred — missed meal, excess insulin?
do_not: Do NOT give anything by mouth if person is unconscious or semi-conscious — choking risk
Do NOT give chocolate or fatty sweets — absorbed too slowly
go_to_hospital_if: Person is unconscious or having seizures
Blood sugar does not rise after 2 rounds of sugar intake
Person is on insulin and had severe episode

immediate_steps: Keep person calm and still — movement spreads venom faster
Immobilise the bitten limb — splint if possible
Remove jewellery, watch, tight clothing near bite area
Mark the swelling boundary with pen and time every 15-30 minutes to monitor spread
Lie person down with bitten limb at or below heart level
Go to nearest hospital IMMEDIATELY — anti-venom is the only effective treatment
do_not: Do NOT cut and suck the wound
Do NOT apply tourniquet
Do NOT apply ice
Do NOT give alcohol
Do NOT use electric shock treatment
go_to_hospital_if: ALL snake bites — go to hospital immediately even if no symptoms yet
source: WHO Snake Bite Management Guidelines India

immediate_steps: Call 108 immediately
If person has an epinephrine auto-injector (EpiPen): use it on outer thigh immediately
Lay person flat with legs elevated UNLESS breathing is difficult — then sit upright
If available and person is conscious: antihistamine (Cetirizine) can help mild symptoms but is NOT a substitute for epinephrine
Be ready to do CPR if person loses consciousness
do_not: Do NOT give water or food
Do NOT let person stand or walk
go_to_hospital_if: This IS an emergency — call 108 immediately
